This is weird take because that is literally the point the movie is making. All the other characters are way worse but because Emma is guilty of "thought crime" they treat her as if she has an infectious disease. The movie is about moralistic self-centering that is less about actual harm done to people but rather about sorting people into good and bad buckets. Instead of empathising with a depressed teenager, instead of considering the circumstances which breed the conditions in which school shootings have become a common occurrence, the characters have a much easier time imagining would-be school shooters as inherently evil. Rachel scoffs at Charlie's suggestion that America has a cultural problem because she would be implicated in that. Instead she decides to place blame on "rotten" individuals.

So, Robert Pattinson's take on Chris Hansen is one of the squirreliest creeps I've ever seen in a movie. The way he recites those explicit online messages to himself as a pre-show mantra is pretty disturbing, and it's literally the last we hear from him. Chris Hansen is ostensibly a journalist, but what exactly is the journalism here? He comes off more like a carnival barker gleefully putting freaks on display for the public to hoot and holler at. By the end of the film, you get the impression that going after predators was Hansen's way of seeking his own level.
